q: Which agency appoints the Building Official of a highly urbanized city?
n: The DPWH Secretary appoints Building Officials, including those of highly urbanized cities. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 205.

q: Which code must the design team consider first, since it is critical to getting a building permit?
n: The National Building Code governs building permits, so the design team must consider it first. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 301.

q: What is any physical change to a building that raises its value or utility or improves its looks?
n: Renovation is any physical change to a building that raises its value, utility or appearance. Source: PD 1096 / NBC IRR, definitions.

q: Under NBC, it is a dwelling containing 2 or more separate living units, each of which is separated from another by party or lot lines walls and provided with independent access:
n: The NBC defines a row house as a dwelling of two or more separate living units, each separated from the next by party or lot-line walls and each with its own independent access. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII (definitions).

q: What is the minimum headroom where a duct crosses a hallway?
n: Where a duct crosses a hallway, at least 2.10 m of unobstructed headroom must remain above the finished floor. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 805.

q: Under the NBC, what is a kitchen's least dimension?
n: A kitchen's least dimension is 1.50 m, with at least 3.00 m² of area. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.

q: Under the NBC, what is a toilet's least dimension?
n: A toilet and bath's least dimension is 0.90 m, with at least 1.20 m² of area. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.

q: Under the NBC, what is the minimum first-storey ceiling height for rooms with natural ventilation?
n: Habitable rooms with natural ventilation need a first-storey ceiling height of at least 2.70 m (2.40 m for the second storey, 2.10 m above). Source: PD 1096, Sec. 805; NBC IRR Rule VIII.

q: Under the NBC, what is the minimum ceiling height of rooms with artificial ventilation?
n: Rooms with artificial ventilation need a ceiling height of at least 2.40 m. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 805; NBC IRR Rule VIII.

q: All on-site work from site preparation, excavation and foundation to assembly and installation of utilities is:
n: Construction covers all on-site work from site preparation, excavation and foundation to assembly of components and installation of utilities. Source: PD 1096 / NBC IRR, definitions.

q: What is the minimum clear width of a stair in a dwelling?
n: A dwelling's stairs need a clear width of at least 0.75 m. Exit stairs serving more than 50 occupants need 1.10 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 708; Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is the maximum distance for the placement of a smoke detector from the door?
n: NFPA 72 spaces smoke detectors about 9.1 m (30 ft) apart on smooth ceilings, so that figure is the basis of the "30" in this item. Source: NFPA 72, Sec. 17.7.3 (spacing); RA 9514 RIRR 2019 (fire detection by reference to NFPA 72).

q: What is the standard height of railings for stairs?
n: Stair handrails are set at about 900 mm above the stair nosing. RA 9514 allows 760–960 mm for stair handrails. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207; RA 9514 RIRR 2019, Sec. 10.2.5.4 H.

q: What is the standard height of railings for landings?
n: Landing rails continue at the stair handrail height, about 900 mm. Guards at open edges are higher. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207; RA 9514 RIRR 2019.

q: R-1 lots allow no firewalls. An abutment for a carport roof is allowed only up to what height?
n: R-1 lots allow no firewalls, but an abutment (such as for a carport roof) up to 3.20 m above established grade may be permitted. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: It is required if the lot owner intends to abut the building to his property line if that side of the lot has an existing neighbor.
n: To abut a building on a property line where a neighbour already exists, a firewall is required. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: The bottom of a window used for emergency egress may be at most how high above the floor?
n: The bottom of a window used for emergency egress may be at most 820 mm (0.82 m) above the floor. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 808.

q: What is the parameter in determining the occupant load for Store Retail in upper floors (Mercantile Establishments)?
n: For upper-floor retail stores (mercantile), the occupant load is figured at 5.60 m² per person. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Table XII.1 (occupant load).

q: A classroom allots 1 m² of floor per student. What ceiling height meets the 3 m³ air space per student?
n: School rooms need 3.00 m³ of air space per pupil. With 1.00 m² of floor per student, the ceiling must be 3.00 m³ ÷ 1.00 m² = 3.00 m. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 807.

q: Under PD 1096, the allowable projection of signage of a building that is not arcaded:
n: On non-arcaded streets, projecting signs may extend at most 1.20 m over the sidewalk from the building line. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XX (signs).

q: As per the code, what is the open space of a corner lot for Group A dwelling?
n: The NBC lets a dwelling occupy at most 90% of a corner lot (80% of an inside lot). The 90% in this item is that occupancy limit, leaving 10% open. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 803.

q: A foundation may encroach into a public sidewalk up to what width (top at least 600 mm below grade)?
n: Footings may project into a public sidewalk up to 500 mm, with their tops at least 600 mm below grade. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule X, Sec. 1002.

q: What determines sidewalk width?
o: The volume of pedestrians using it regularly
n: Sidewalk width is set by the volume of pedestrians who regularly use it. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule X; Fruin, Pedestrian Planning and Design.

q: What is the minimum air space per occupant in school rooms?
o: 3.00 m³ with 1.00 m² of floor per person
n: School rooms require at least 3.00 m³ of air space with 1.00 m² of floor area per person. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 807.

q: What is the standard ceiling height for habitable rooms, kitchens, utility rooms, etc.?
n: For habitable rooms and kitchens, the commonly used minimum ceiling height is 2.40 m (with artificial ventilation). Naturally ventilated first storeys need 2.70 m. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 805.

q: Under NBC Sec. 401, what is Type III construction?
n: Type III construction is masonry and wood, with structural elements of at least one-hour fire-resistive rating. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 401.

q: What is the minimum height of a T&B door according to the NBC?
n: Doors, including those of toilets and baths, must be at least 2.00 m high. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is the minimum width of an aisle serving one side only?
n: An aisle serving seats on one side only must be at least 0.80 m wide. Corridors are at least 1.10 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is not the recommended height of an entrance opening?
n: Entrance openings should be at least 2.00 m high (2.10 m is common). A 1.50 m opening is below the minimum door height, so it is not recommended. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What section in the NBC states the exemptions for applying for a building permit?
n: Section 209 of the NBC sets out the exemptions from building permits. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 209.

q: What section in the NBC states the non-issuance, suspension, and revocation of building permits?
n: Section 306 covers non-issuance, suspension and revocation of building permits. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 306.

q: Which NBC Rule covers classification and general requirements of buildings by use or occupancy?
n: Rule VII of the NBC IRR covers classification and general requirements of buildings by use or occupancy. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII.

q: What section in the NBC states the maximum height of buildings?
n: Section 707 sets the maximum height of buildings. It limits building height through the Building Height Limit set for each use or zone. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 707.

q: Which NBC Rule covers light and ventilation?
n: Rule VIII covers light and ventilation. It covers windows, courts, ceiling heights, room sizes and ventilation requirements. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII.

q: Which NBC section covers percentage of site occupancy?
n: Section 803 covers the percentage of site occupancy. It sets the maximum share of a lot a building may occupy, by lot type. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 803.

q: Which NBC section covers ceiling heights?
n: Section 805 covers ceiling heights. It sets minimum ceiling heights for habitable rooms by storey and type of ventilation. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 805.

q: Which NBC section covers types of construction?
n: Section 401 covers types of construction (Types I–V). It classifies buildings into Types I–V according to the fire resistance of their structural elements. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 401.

q: Which NBC Rule covers fire zones?
n: Rule V covers fire zones and fire-resistive standards. It covers the designation of fire zones and the buildings and fire-resistive standards required in each. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule V.

q: What is the maximum riser of an exit stair under the NBC?
n: Exit stairs may have a maximum riser of 200 mm. Uniform, moderate risers let occupants descend quickly and safely during an emergency. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is the minimum run (tread) of an exit stair under the NBC?
n: Exit stairs need a minimum tread (run) of 250 mm, excluding nosing. Dwelling stairs allow less. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is the minimum window opening for a habitable room?
n: Habitable rooms need window openings of at least 10% of the floor area (natural light and ventilation). Source: PD 1096, Sec. 808.

q: How long is a building permit valid if work hasn't started?
n: A building permit lapses if work does not start within 12 months of issuance. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 305.

q: A permit also expires if work is abandoned or suspended after it starts for:
n: A permit also expires if work is suspended or abandoned for 120 days after it starts. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 305.

q: What slope should a driveway entry ramp from the roadway to the sidewalk have?
n: A driveway entry ramp from the roadway across the curb to the sidewalk should slope about 1:3 to 1:4. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule X (sidewalk and driveway guidelines).

q: The NBC gives a framework of ______ standards and requirements for all buildings.
n: The NBC provides a framework of minimum standards and requirements for all buildings. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 102.
